decisionsTitle: The volunteers' page: each category its own card, each role a tile
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-15, on a screenshot of «Vreau să fiu voluntar la …»:** the intro, «Ce ești dispus(ă) să faci», then «Activități start/finish» and «Pe Traseu» as plain headings, each role a bare checkbox with a small «mai sunt locuri» line under the box, one long flat list — «Și aici aș vrea mai multe separatoare și un design mai frumos pentru roluri», and then, emphatic: «nu e clară gruparea pe categorii! vreau să prioritizezi asta!».

**Decision (amending §768 and §774; the fields, the server rules, the counts and the gates are untouched).** The test of the design is one question, asked of a screenshot at 320 px: must a reader ever wonder which category a role belongs to? So each category is **a card of its own** (`VolunteerCategoryCard`): a bordered, rounded box with a band across its top in the primary colour and its own contrast text (`primary.contrastText`, AA in both colour schemes and both looks, «Tema v1» and «Tema v2»), holding the house's volunteers glyph, the category's name large as the level-3 heading the group is named by, and how many roles it offers («1 rol», «4 roluri», «20 de roluri» — `Event.volunteers.roleCount`, the three forms of `countForm`); under the band the category's contact line (§774) when the club set one, then its roles. Between two cards stands a clear step (24 px on a phone), and «Alte activități» is last with the same look. The role is inside the box under the band, never between two headings, so the grouping reads before a word of it is read. An event with no category draws the tiles under no heading and in no card, as before. The instruction line stays above the first card and the owner's note (§773) under the last.

Each role is **a tile** (`VolunteerRoleTile`): the house's selectable card, whose surface — the two-pixel border, the primary border and light tint on `:checked`, the keyboard ring on `:focus-visible`, all in CSS through `:has` — was the feedback page's `BranchChoice` (§676) and is now shared (`src/shared/ui/choice-card.ts`: `CHOICE_CARD_SX`, `CHOICE_INPUT_SX`, `paletteWash`, which moved out of the feedback module; `BranchChoice` draws with the shared object, its look unchanged). The tile's whole surface is the checkbox's `<label>` (at least 44 px tall), around a native checkbox named `roleIds`, the role's name and, **under the name** (not under the box), the count line («mai sunt locuri» / «mai e nevoie de N persoane», §773). The box is named by the role's name alone (`aria-labelledby`) and described by the count line and the description. The role's description (§765) sits under the name **outside the label**: it may hold a link and a native fold («Detalii»), and a label may not hold either, so a press on the description reads or opens it and never ticks the role (`RoleDescription` takes `flush`, the tile indenting it). The tiles are a grid of one column at a phone's width and two from the tablet's (`minmax(0, 1fr)` so a long name wraps inside its tile). The ticked state is the tile's primary border and tint together with the box's own mark, never colour alone.

**No script, no island.** Both components are Server Components over native inputs, so the page works with scripts off and a refused post comes back with its ticks from the sealed draft (§142, §315) exactly as before: the form is a plain Server Action form, so the recall context is empty here and `typed.roleIds` is the whole of it. The band holds no link (the contact line's links sit on the card's surface under it), so the primary band is safe in both looks.

**Refused.** A white card with only a divider above each heading (the brief's first idea) — the band is what makes the grouping obvious at a glance on a phone; a client island for the ticked state — CSS `:has` does it; a new card component for the tile — the feedback page's surface is shared instead; a second glyph per category — one volunteers glyph for all, the name tells them apart; a link or fold inside the label — invalid HTML.
changelogLine: - **The volunteers' page: each category its own card, each role a tile** — a bordered card per category with a coloured band (glyph, name, «4 roluri») and the contact line, the roles inside it as tiles whose whole surface ticks the box, the count line under the name, two columns from the tablet width, working with scripts off. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criterion 43. Given an event whose roles sit under categories, when a visitor opens `/ro/evenimente/<slug>/voluntari`, then each category is a card of its own — a band with its glyph, its name as the level-3 heading and the number of roles it offers («1 rol», «4 roluri»), its contact line under the band when set, its roles inside as tiles — with clear empty space between two cards and «Alte activități» last with the same look, and an event with no category shows its tiles under no heading and in no card; each role is a tile whose whole surface is the checkbox's label, at least 44 pixels tall, so a press on its count line ticks the box, with the count line under the role's name, the description outside the label (folded «Detalii» when long), the ticked tile drawn with the primary border and tint, one column at 320 pixels and two from the tablet width, no horizontal scroll, native inputs only so that it works with scripts off and a refused post comes back with the roles ticked (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the volunteers' page: each category its own card, roles as tiles
